title: Credit / blame attribution record (Phase 6 Step 6)
description: One focused record per canonical article: WHO receives credit or blame, for WHAT, assigned BY WHOM - responsibility attribution as the article reports it, never inferred. Electoral consequence prediction and voter-switching analysis are OUT of scope for this step by specification.

schema_version.description: v1.1 adds target_type politician (pilot finding: national articles attribute to individual politicians who are not local candidates); v1.0 records remain valid under their own stamp

attributions.description: one row per distinct (target, outcome) attribution the article carries

attribution_type.description: mixed only when the SAME attribution carries both directions; separate praise and criticism are separate rows

target_type.description: politician (v1.1): a named national/individual politician who is not a local candidate in the studied elections

source_type.description: who ASSIGNS the blame/credit - the article's own narration is 'journalist'; a quoted rival is 'politician'

source_name.description: the named assigner when the article names one (e.g. the quoted councillor); null for unnamed sources or pure narration

attributed_outcome.description: WHAT is being attributed - the event, decision or outcome

reasoning.description: WHY the target receives blame/credit, per the article - the audit trail

affected_issue.description: issues-v1.3 code linking this attribution to the issue layer; null when no code fits

electoral_implication.description: the possible electoral reading AS THE ARTICLE SUGGESTS IT - descriptive only, never a prediction; required by rule C4 when implication_direction is not 'unclear'

implication_direction.description: whether this attribution may damage or benefit the target politically
